Only one plate is the meal; the small crumb on the table at left is not part of it.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A large square white dinner plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area = 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2 (square plate, so slightly more usable area, but I use the round approximation).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Sliced pink-centered meat (roast beef/steak slices) on the right side
- Dark brown browned chunks (roasted vegetable or meat pieces) in the center-left
- Light brown sauce or juice smears on the plate (negligible)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Sliced meat: ~15% of vessel (about 80 cm^2)
- Dark brown chunks: ~12% (about 64 cm^2)
- Total food coverage ≈ 27%, consistent with the visible portion of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume (outer envelope):
- Meat slices: 80 cm^2 x 1.0 cm = 80 ml
- Brown chunks: 64 cm^2 x 2.0 cm = 128 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Meat: 80 ml x 0.95 = 76 g
- Chunks (treated as dense roasted meat/vegetable mix): 128 ml x 0.9 = 115 g

STEP 7 - Energy (cooked weight):
- Roast beef, cooked: ~250 kcal/100 g → 76 g → 190 kcal
- Brown chunks, assumed roasted root vegetable with fat/glaze: ~120 kcal/100 g → 115 g → 138 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Visible food is a modest portion, covering about a quarter of a dinner plate, so roughly 190 g total is plausible. Total ≈ 190 g, ≈ 330 kcal.
